text:
Sam: Heads-up — quick check on selector contract changes in the policy runtime. Thinking about shrinking the decision payload we send to edge deciders. Current payload: route_id, tenant, seq_len, cost_hint, latency_budget, region_pref, model_fingerprint, allowed_variants. Proposal: drop allowed_variants and instead send variant_class hint + compatibility bitmap. Would reduce size ~30% and make sidecars simpler. Thoughts?
Anya: Sounds promising. How do you plan to encode the bitmap? could get messy with model rollout churn.
Sam: Bitmap is per-variant-feature (quantized/float16/kvcache) not per-version. So it's stable across small model revs.
Dario: Simulation wise we should validate that no tenant relies on explicit allowed_variants to do strict filtering. Any consumers that expect a whitelist semantics?
Maria: Customer-facing fallbacks rely on explicit allowed lists today for compliance customers. We can't silently change semantics.
Kai: Ops question — telemetry: if we move to compact hints, will we lose explanatory fields for debug + metrics? We need traceability to reconstruct why a decision was made.
Sam: Good point. Proposal is: compact runtime payload + append a signed decision_provenance blob back to control plane (async) for expensive traces. Control plane keeps the full expanded form for audits.
Anya: That sounds OK but increases operational load on control plane. How expensive is the blob?
Sam: Small — mostly key-value pairs, base64 of the original allowed_variants only when request triggers a fallback. Default is empty.
Dario: We should add a simulation run: 1) convert historical traffic, 2) run refactored selector locally, 3) flag any mismatch where old runtime allowed request but new compact selector rejects it.
Maria: Also add a canary flag for compliance tenants — keep full payload for them during rollout.
Kai: +1 on canary. For debugging, keep the decision_id in payload so sidecars can ask control plane for full dump.
Sam: Plan sketch in proto form:
```proto
message SelectorHint {
  string tenant = 1;
  string route_id = 2;
  uint32 seq_len = 3;
  float cost_hint = 4;
  uint32 latency_budget_ms = 5;
  repeated string region_pref = 6;
  bytes model_fingerprint = 7;
  VariantClass variant_class = 8; // enum: STANDARD, LOW_PREC, KVCACHE
  bytes compat_bitmap = 9; // bitset of feature compatibilities
  string decision_id = 10;
}
```
Dario: Lgtm. For compat_bitmap semantics, let's add a version number so we can rotate encoding without hardfail.
Sam: Agreed. We'll add compat_schema_version uint32.
Anya: Who owns migration? Runtime team or policy team? This touches both.
Sam: Runtime implements decoding + shallow validation. Policy team owns schema and backward compatibility guarantees.
Maria: Rollout checklist suggestion: 1) simulation gap <0.01% 2) canary for 2w on compliance tenants 3) telemetry dashboards for mismatch reasons 4) automated rollback on >0.1% errors.
Kai: Add a small panic-safe path: if sidecar fails to decode bitmap, it should treat as permissive (best-effort) and emit an alert. Prefer availability over unexpected rejections.
Anya: Permissive default is usually safer but could violate strict compliance. That's why canary + per-tenant full payload is needed.
Sam: I'll draft an RFC addendum with proto diff + migration plan + simulation harness. Also include a small python script to convert historical logs.
Maria: Thanks. Can you add a note about retention of decision_provenance for audits (30-90d)? compliance wants 90d.
Sam: Will do, default 90d for compliance tenants, 30d for others.
ops-bot: FYI: staging cluster deploy window open 03/14 02:00-04:00 UTC.
deploy-bot: Canaries scheduled after staging verification. Will ping #release-war-room when ready.
Dario: One more ask — include a cheap checksum in compat_bitmap so corruptions are obvious without round-tripping.
Sam: Good call. I'll include a CRC32 field.
Maria: Ok if you post the RFC here when ready we'll review and kick off simulation runs. :thumbsup:
